verdict.rationale: Yubico ships its own programmatic surfaces for the key: the official ykman CLI offers scriptable device management (applications, PINs, PIV/OATH/OTP slots, device info), and the .NET SDK integrates the key and its applications into code. The docs name the GUI and ykman as alternatives for at least one task (reading firmware version), but nothing states that every UI action is available programmatically. missing for 10: explicit documentation of API/CLI parity with the Yubico Authenticator GUI, a machine-readable API spec (OpenAPI probes 404), and independent hands-on confirmation that all GUI functions can be scripted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Full scriptable device management: enable applications, PINs, PIV/OATH/OTP slots, device info.
Configure your YubiKey via the command line.
use either the Yubico Authenticator with its intuitive and easy-to-use (GUI) interface or ykman
The SDK allows you to integrate the YubiKey and its applications into your .NET-based application or library.
